expected: Measured peak RAM/VRAM/disk, startup and failures; conservative reproducible fit.
limitations: Host timestamps are retained as recorded; the host clock was about 41 s behind real time.
The GPU also drives a display (profile display_attached). The interactive desktop was signed out, but two WDDM graphics clients remain; no foreign compute tenant was observed.
On this 64 GiB host stock setup gives IQ3_S no KV streaming: the KV cache stays in VRAM and the expert arena is in RAM (46.84 GiB loaded according to the engine log).
The GPU link is x8 of a host-visible Gen3 x16 maximum; this is not a fresh OS.
Serving-state commit available was only 719548416 bytes against an 83608145920-byte limit. This is tight headroom, not evidence of a comfortable margin or an indefinite stability guarantee.
Per-process lifetime peaks describe the tree alive at each measurement, not a full-run sampled peak. Resource sampling can miss transient peaks; evaluation-specific peak RAM/VRAM are unavailable.
Only G10, G17 and the final G21 snapshot supplied resource samples. Fault, lifecycle and long-session gates were not run; zero error-pattern matches do not prove indefinite stability.
observed: At the final G21 sample, current engine lifetime peaks are 52752326656 bytes working set and 78394593280 bytes private commit. Earlier G17 observed 52888604672 and 78528192512 bytes respectively in a previous engine generation. Recorded gate samples peak at 23439 MiB GPU use and reach 9211936768 bytes minimum available RAM. Five server logs contain 292 completed requests and no engine-error/OOM/CUDA-error/traceback/watchdog-stop matches, unexpected engine restart, disconnect or error-ended request. This is the bounded resource record of the exploratory run, not candidate qualification.
